operations.label: PCR / dsOligo-specific amplification
operations.description: PCR uses the integrated tag and sequencing-adapter interfaces to enrich tag-associated genomic fragments and produce indexed sequencing-library DNA. The primer schematic and following arrow to final DNA belong to this broad amplification block; no additional independent assay is implied.
operations.mechanism: The paper calls the component Single-Tail Adapter/Tag (STAT)-PCR: a tag-complementary primer and an adapter-complementary primer support selective unidirectional amplification of a genomic flank. It reports two rounds of nested anchored PCR and primers addressing both tag strands.
operations.information_effect: Enriches captured tag–genome junctions over untagged background. Sequencing the adjacent genomic DNA allows mapping to integration sites and hence localization of captured DSBs; the primary figure describes localization within a few base pairs. The molecular index supports consolidation of PCR copies of original DNA fragments. Captured insertion sites are the readout, rather than direct indel measurements or nuclease binding. Tag delivery/capture, recovery and sequencing limit representation: missing sites cannot establish absence of cleavage, and captured background breaks need not be RGN-induced. Sequencing and mapping are the reported downstream interpretation, not separately depicted operations.
